_about: Public CMS Picker settings, read by `python build\playbook.py publish`. Every answer, each platform's profile and logo, and which platforms are public live in the picker table (admins edit them on the Playbook's CMS Picker tab), separate from the Playbook's own answers. `platforms` here is the display order; other public platforms follow by name. Each row's label finishes "Can you…" in plain words; "term" is the SEO name shown small under it. `quiz` holds the guided quiz's own judgements per platform (the rest of its scoring comes from the answers and profiles). The "cost" section shows each platform's cheapest way to start, as a band from its own pricing page (answers use the cost tags: free, low, mid, high, software, na), with the month it was checked as "asOf".

quiz._about: Find my fit. ease: how easy it is to run without technical skills (0 needs a developer, 3 easiest). look: the design control it suits (template = start from a theme, visual = arrange pages yourself, pixel = every detail). largeCatalogue / smallShop: stores it suits. storeOnly: only for selling, so marked down for anything else. agency: a common choice for designers and agencies; agencyOnly: mostly sold through them. customFrontEnd: built to feed an app or any front end. devControl: built to be coded, so a developer gets full control (picked when "A developer" builds it). domainDocs: the platform's own help page for connecting your own domain (official docs only, checked 2026-10-29; none for self-hosted Drupal or headless), linked from the first steps on a result. kind: for business or work sites, which platforms suit each answer to "Which is closest to what you do?" (from each platform's "good fit" lines: local businesses and services, creative work, startups, B2B companies, lots of content). members: for blogs and publications, the platforms with paid memberships and newsletters built in (from their published profiles). b2b: stores whose profiles name selling to other businesses (wholesale, trade accounts, bulk orders): BigCommerce ("B2B tools") and Magento ("Enterprise and B2B stores"). bigStoresOnly: built for large or complex stores, so marked down for a small shop (Magento: its card says "Less suited if you run a small shop"). Checked 2026-10-29: visual arranging on WordPress (block editor), Shopify (theme editor sections), BigCommerce (Page Builder), HubSpot (drag-and-drop editor) and Drupal (Canvas, default in Drupal CMS 2.0); HubSpot ease 2 as marketers build pages on its themes without code. sanity (2026-10-29): replaces the Headless CMS category on the CMS Picker; the same values, since it needs a developer and feeds any front end. No domainDocs: the website's host connects the domain. addOnsMany / addOnsSome (2026-10-30, for "Will you add features as the site grows?"): the size of each platform's plugin or app library. Many (tens of thousands): WordPress's plugin directory, Drupal's modules (about 50,000), Shopify's App Store (12,000 to 25,000 by tracker). Some (about a thousand or more): Magento (Adobe Commerce Marketplace, about 3,700), BigCommerce (over 1,000), HubSpot (App Marketplace). Fewer: Wix (hundreds), Webflow (300+), Squarespace, Framer, Ghost, Duda; Sanity is built by a developer, so add-ons are code. Counts are third-party estimates where the platform gives none; the tiers are far apart, so they hold. 2026-10-30 (round 5): Wix joins addOnsSome (its App Market has no published total; about 800 by third-party count, the same range as BigCommerce's "Over 1,200 apps", and "App market" is a known-for tag); Squarespace stays out (about 55 extensions on its own Extensions page); Shopify's App Store says "over 16,000 apps". crmFirst: built around its own CRM, so marked down for local businesses and creatives (HubSpot's card: less suited if you don't otherwise use HubSpot).
